title: The Fawn and His Mother
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Hind said to her Fawn, who was now well grown and strong, "My son, Nature has given you a powerful body and a stout pair of horns, and I can't think why you are such a coward as to run away from the hounds." Just then they both heard the sound of a pack in full cry, but at a considerable distance. "You stay where you are," said the Hind; "never mind me": and with that she ran off as fast as her legs could carry her.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who is speaking to the Fawn at the start of the passage?
options: His mother, the Hind
A passing hunter
Another, older fawn
A hound from a nearby pack

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what has Nature given the Fawn?
options: A powerful body and a stout pair of horns
A keen sense of smell and sharp eyesight
Great speed but a weak body
Thick fur and a loud voice

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Hind accuse the Fawn of being?
options: A coward for running from the hounds
Too lazy to graze properly
Disobedient toward his mother
Careless around strangers

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Hind and Fawn hear just after her accusation?
options: A pack in full cry, at a considerable distance
A loud crash nearby
Another deer calling for help
A hunter's horn very close by

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Hind tell the Fawn to do once they hear the pack?
options: To stay where he is
To hide behind a tree at once
To follow her closely
To call out for help

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Hind do immediately after telling the Fawn not to mind her?
options: She ran off as fast as her legs could carry her
She turned to face the approaching hounds
She stayed beside the Fawn protectively
She called out to other deer for help

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "pack in full cry" mean in "they both heard the sound of a pack in full cry"?
options: A group of hounds baying loudly while in pursuit
A herd of deer calling to each other
A crowd of hunters shouting commands
A flock of birds startled into flight

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why is it ironic that the Hind flees immediately after calling her Fawn a coward?
options: She proves by her own action that fear of the hounds is reasonable, not cowardly
She realizes the Fawn was right to be afraid the whole time
She was only testing the Fawn's courage
She was actually fleeing from a different danger entirely

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the passage describe the Fawn's condition at the start?
options: Well grown and strong
Small and sickly
Newly born
Injured from a recent chase

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what exact words does the Hind say just before she runs off?
options: "You stay where you are," "never mind me"
"Follow me closely, my son"
"We must fight together"
"It is too late to escape now"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how far away was the pack when the Hind and Fawn first heard it?
options: At a considerable distance
Right beside them
Just over a nearby hill, very close
The passage does not say

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "stout" mean in "a stout pair of horns"?
options: Sturdy and strong
Thin and fragile
Newly grown
Oddly shaped

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Hind's own behavior suggest about the advice she gave the Fawn?
options: Her advice does not match how she herself responds to real danger
Her advice was proven correct by her own calm response
She wanted the Fawn to imitate her exact actions
She had never actually faced hounds before this moment

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Hind mocks her Fawn for fearing hounds, then flees herself the moment hounds are heard
A Hind teaches her Fawn to fight off a pack of hounds
A Fawn abandons his mother when hounds approach
A Hind and her Fawn work together to scare off a pack of hounds
